ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a rectangular flip-flop symbol, with the upper input on the left labeled J, the lower input on the left labeled K, and a CP clock input symbol in the middle on the left; the upper output on the right is labeled Q, and the lower output on the right also has a complementary output terminal with a small circle. Inside the rectangle, markings related to J, K, and the clock can be seen, such as 1J, C1, and 1K. Reasoning: Since the control input terminals of this flip-flop are clearly labeled J and K, it is a JK flip-flop. The next state of a JK flip-flop consists of two parts: when the current state Q^n is 0 and J=1, it is set, corresponding to the term J\overline{Q}^n; when the current state Q^n is 1 and K=0, it remains 1, corresponding to the term \overline{K}Q^n. Adding the two terms gives the characteristic equation: Q^{n+1}=J\overline{Q}^n+\overline{K}Q^n.
